newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Brambles yr net seen rising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Brambles yr net seen rising.

text.p: Transport, security and industrial services group Brambles Industries Ltd, bolstered by healthy earnings from its U.S. pallet joint venture Chep, is expected to report a stronger pre-abnormal net profit for year to June 30.

Analysts contacted by Reuters forecasted Brambles would report a pre-abnormal net profit of A$208 million to A$214 million for the year, a rise of between 12 and 15 percent on the A$185.52 million the company reported in the 1994/95 year.
"Brambles wanted to achieve a record profit last year and I think they will achieve it," said Ian Myles, transport analyst at Macquarie Equities.
Myles forecast Brambles to report a pre-abnormal net profit of A$214 million for the 1996/97 year.
In February, Brambles said it was on track for a solid profit increase for the year to June 30, 1996.
"We expect Australian earnings year-on-year to better the percentage increase at the half-year," Brambles managing director John Fletcher said.
Analysts said one of the key factors driving Brambles strong earnings was the growth of its U.S. pallet joint venture, Chep.
Earlier this month British industrial group GKN Plc, which owns the other 50 percent of Chep U.S., reported strong half year earnings and said the Chep business was partly responsible for its gains.
"GKN's results confirmed that Chep U.S. is up to about 16 million pallets and Chep Europe up to 39 million pallets," one Sydney-based analyst said.
GKN said in the last year the Chep U.S. pallet pool had grown by a third and there was considerable growth potential in both South America and Asia.
Brambles shares closed eight cents higher at A$18.78 on Wednesday.
Its shares have risen about 41 percent since June 30, 1995.
